data.name: Eddy紫 ~Eddy Violet~
data.detailed_description:
"Eddy Violet" is an Dreampunk and Postcyberpunk-based ACT game developed in the span of two years. I finished all the sections of game design by myself including 30 pieces of original music. The game is finished in my sophomore year, 2012. After 5 years, finally got a chance to publish a Steam version!
Six levels and bosses, five mini games and hardcore platformer all in one, I’m trying to bring the players a novel visual and intriguing narrative in play.



--- Story ---
The Great Mother eliminated the old world, re-established new order upon the science civilization’s ruins. She has been creating numerous energy-state lives and led the world to the completely new ecosystem.
But the Great Mother can’t destroy her own creations, which means that if those creatures rise in rebellion, god would feel helpless and the new world would return to chaos.

Eddy – the girl soldier of “Vortex Guardian” who have a half-energy and half-human body – is responsible for the peace of Beij District where the center of new world is located. Depending on her rapid recovery ability of Vortex Guardian, Eddy has extirpated a lot of enemies who was trying to overturn rules of the Great Mother.

However, at this time, an extreme dangerous usurper is coming from the horizon…


Features:
-Wonderful game world & art style
-Creative energy-bullet-color-counteracting game play
-Custom skills, weapons and armor upgrade system
-6 levels with powerful bosses
-6 unique mini-games to play through
-More than 36 hidden items waiting for being collected
-30 pieces of original background music
-Only 1 author ;P
English version is upcoming!

reviews.review:
Eddy Violet is a highly individualistic action-adventure title that reflects the ambition and personal vision of its sole creator, 大谷 DGSpitzer, who both developed and published the game. Rather than adhering to familiar genre formulas or modern indie trends, the game blends retro arcade influences with science-fiction worldbuilding, platforming challenges, RPG-like progression ideas, and experimental mechanics into a compact but surprisingly layered experience. From the outset, it is clear that Eddy Violet is less concerned with accessibility or mass appeal and more focused on expressing a distinct creative identity.

The game is set in a surreal sci-fi universe shaped by catastrophe and renewal, where energy-based lifeforms coexist uneasily with remnants of human civilization. Players step into the role of Eddy, a hybrid being who exists somewhere between human and energy, serving as a guardian tasked with suppressing unrest and restoring balance in a fractured district. The narrative is delivered sparingly and often indirectly, acting more as thematic context than as a driving force. Instead of lengthy exposition, the world is communicated through visual motifs, enemy designs, and environmental details, leaving much of the interpretation to the player.

Gameplay centers on fast-paced 2D action that draws heavily from classic run-and-gun and bullet-hell traditions. Eddy moves through a series of stages filled with enemies that fire dense, colorful projectile patterns, demanding constant movement and sharp reflexes. A key mechanic revolves around color-based interactions between attacks and defenses, where understanding how different energy types counter or amplify each other becomes essential for survival. This system elevates combat beyond simple shooting and dodging, encouraging players to read patterns carefully and adapt positioning and timing to mitigate damage.

Each level culminates in a boss encounter designed as a skill check that combines everything learned up to that point. These fights emphasize pattern recognition and endurance, often pushing players to the limits of their situational awareness. While challenging, the bosses are generally fair, rewarding persistence and observation rather than brute force. Outside of combat-heavy segments, the game introduces hardcore platforming sections and assorted mini-games that shift the pace and test precision in different ways, adding variety and preventing the experience from becoming monotonous.

Progression in Eddy Violet is relatively understated but meaningful within its scope. Hidden items and optional challenges reward exploration and careful play, encouraging multiple attempts at stages to uncover everything they offer. While the game does not feature deep character builds or extensive customization, the gradual increase in difficulty and mechanical complexity provides a sense of growth rooted in player skill rather than numerical upgrades.

Visually, the game stands out through its distinctive pixel-art style infused with surreal and dreampunk-inspired imagery. Environments feel otherworldly, blending mechanical structures with dreamlike elements that reinforce the game’s abstract tone. The art may appear rough or unconventional at times, but it is cohesive and expressive, clearly driven by a singular artistic vision. Complementing the visuals is a substantial original soundtrack composed by the developer, featuring energetic and atmospheric tracks that heighten tension during combat and lend emotional weight to quieter moments.

Despite its creativity, Eddy Violet is not without limitations. One of the most notable barriers is its lack of full English localization, which can make narrative elements and menus difficult to understand for non-Chinese-speaking players. Additionally, as a largely solo-developed project, the game occasionally shows technical roughness, such as inconsistent performance or control quirks during particularly busy sequences. These issues do not define the experience, but they do remind players of the game’s indie roots.

Community reception has generally been positive, especially among players who appreciate experimental indie games and are willing to overlook rough edges in favor of originality. Many highlight the inventive mechanics, memorable bosses, and striking soundtrack as standout features, while criticism tends to focus on accessibility and polish rather than core design. The game’s reputation reflects its niche appeal: it resonates strongly with a specific audience rather than attempting to satisfy everyone.

Ultimately, Eddy Violet is a game driven by creative conviction rather than convention. It offers a challenging, mechanically interesting action experience wrapped in an unusual sci-fi aesthetic that feels deeply personal. While its quirks and barriers may limit its reach, players who enjoy retro-inspired action games, bullet-hell mechanics, and indie projects with strong artistic identity will find Eddy Violet to be a memorable and rewarding journey that stands apart from more formulaic titles.

Rating: 6/10
